description: Manage a FortiGate firewall: block and unblock IP addresses, keep address groups and policies up to date, check interfaces, VPN tunnels, routes, DHCP leases, firmware and logs, back up the configuration, and start workflows on security events, sign-in failures, configuration changes and links or tunnels going down.

fortinet_fortigate_admin_login_failed_tr.description: Runs when someone fails to sign in to the FortiGate as an administrator, with the name they tried and where from. Failures before the workflow is turned on don't start it. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.interface: How they tried, such as https(203.0.113.10) or ssh(203.0.113.10).
output.method: The sign-in method, such as https or ssh.
output.reason: Why it failed, such as name_invalid or passwd_invalid.
output.source_ip: The address the attempt came from.
output.user: The administrator name that was tried.

parameters.description: Where the FortiGate keeps its logs: memory (the default) or disk, for models with a log disk.
parameters.name: source

fortinet_fortigate_config_changed_trigge.description: Runs when an administrator changes the FortiGate's configuration, with who changed what. Changes made before the workflow is turned on don't start it. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.action: What they did: Add, Edit or Delete.
output.attributes: The settings changed and their new values.
output.interface: Where they made it, such as GUI(203.0.113.10) or the REST API.
output.object: The entry changed, such as a policy's ID.
output.path: The settings path changed, such as firewall.policy.
output.user: The administrator who made the change.

parameters.description: Only changes whose settings path contains this text, such as firewall.policy or system.admin. Leave blank for every change.
parameters.name: path_contains

parameters.description: Where the FortiGate keeps its logs: memory (the default) or disk, for models with a log disk.
parameters.name: source

fortinet_fortigate_firmware_available_tr.description: Runs when FortiGuard offers a FortiOS version newer than the one the FortiGate runs. Versions already offered when the workflow is turned on don't start it. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.current_version: The version the FortiGate runs now.
output.version: The new version, such as v7.4.5.

fortinet_fortigate_interface_down_trigge.description: Runs when one of the FortiGate's interfaces loses its link. Interfaces already down when the workflow is turned on don't start it, and one starts it again each time it goes down. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.name: The interface's name, such as wan1.

parameters.description: Only this interface. Leave blank for every interface.
parameters.name: interface

fortinet_fortigate_ip_banned_trigger.description: Runs when the FortiGate bans (quarantines) an IP address, by intrusion prevention, a DoS policy or an administrator. Bans already there when the workflow is turned on don't start it. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.expires: When the ban ends (ISO 8601, UTC), empty when permanent.
output.ipv6: Whether it is an IPv6 address.
output.permanent: Whether the ban lasts until removed.
output.source: What banned it, such as ips, dos or admin.

fortinet_fortigate_new_dhcp_lease_trigge.description: Runs when the FortiGate's DHCP server hands an address to a device, such as a new device joining the network. Leases already there when the workflow is turned on don't start it. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.hostname: The device's host name, if it gave one.
output.interface: The interface the DHCP server is on.
output.reserved: Whether the address is reserved for this device.
output.status: The lease's status, such as leased.
output.vendor_class: The device's vendor class, if it sent one.

parameters.description: Only leases on this interface. Leave blank for every interface.
parameters.name: interface

fortinet_fortigate_new_event_log_trigger.description: Runs for each new entry in one of the FortiGate's event logs, such as system, VPN or user events. Entries already there when the workflow is turned on don't start it. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.date: The date, as the FortiGate writes it.
output.details: Every other field of the entry.
output.dstip: The destination IP address, if any.
output.eventtime: When it happened, in FortiOS's own units since 1970.
output.level: Its level, such as information, warning or alert.
output.logdesc: What kind of event it is, such as Admin login successful.
output.logid: The log message's ID, such as 0100032001.
output.srcip: The source IP address, if any.
output.type: The log type, such as event.

parameters.description: Which event log to watch: system (System), user (User authentication), vpn (VPN), router (Routing), ha (High availability), wireless (Wireless), endpoint (Endpoint control), security-rating (Security rating). Defaults to system.
parameters.name: log_type

parameters.description: Where the FortiGate keeps its logs: memory (the default) or disk, for models with a log disk.
parameters.name: source

fortinet_fortigate_new_policy_trigger.description: Runs when a firewall policy is added to the FortiGate, with what it matches and does. Policies already there when the workflow is turned on don't start it. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.logtraffic: What it logs: all, utm or disable.
output.name: Its name.

fortinet_fortigate_security_event_trigge.description: Runs when the FortiGate logs a security event, such as an intrusion attempt, a virus or a blocked website, with its source, destination and threat. Events before the workflow is turned on don't start it. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.action: What the FortiGate did, such as dropped, blocked or passthrough.
output.event_type: Its event type, such as signature or infected.
output.level: Its level or severity, such as alert or high.
output.policy_id: The ID of the policy the traffic matched.
output.threat: The attack, virus, application or category named.
output.type: The kind of event, such as ips, virus or webfilter.
output.url: The URL or host name, for web and DNS events.

parameters.description: Which security log to watch: ips (Intrusion prevention), virus (Antivirus), webfilter (Web filter), app-ctrl (Application control), anomaly (Anomaly), dns (DNS filter). Defaults to ips.
parameters.name: log_type

parameters.description: Where the FortiGate keeps its logs: memory (the default) or disk, for models with a log disk.
parameters.name: source

fortinet_fortigate_vpn_tunnel_down_trigg.description: Runs when an IPsec VPN tunnel goes down. Tunnels already down when the workflow is turned on don't start it, and one starts it again each time it goes down. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

parameters.description: Only the tunnel with this name. Leave blank for every tunnel.
parameters.name: tunnel
